blogs.title: The 'False Positive' CA-125 in Pregnancy: When Benign Myomas Mimic Ovarian Malignancy
blogs.description: This post dissects the diagnostic dilemma of elevated tumor markers in pregnant patients. Using the case of a patient with a CA-125 level of 41.8 U/mL, we explore why relying on standard cut-offs (<35 U/mL) leads to unnecessary anxiety and potential overtreatment. We review the physiological peaks of CA-125 across trimesters and discuss how decidualization, endometriosis, and large leiomyomas can cause false-positive elevations, emphasizing the need for multimodal imaging over serology alone.

blogs.title: To Cut or Not to Cut? Navigating the Surgical Dilemma of Large Intrathoracic Leiomyomas in the Second Trimester
blogs.description: Surgical intervention during pregnancy carries significant risks of miscarriage and preterm labor, yet conservative management can lead to catastrophic complications like torsion or respiratory failure. This article analyzes the decision-making process for a patient with massive uterine leiomyomas causing dyspnea and pain. We discuss the indications for urgent mid-trimester myomectomy versus expectant management, focusing on balancing maternal symptom relief against fetal safety.

blogs.title: Imaging Without Contrast: Optimizing MRI Protocols for Complex Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: When ultrasound yields ambiguous results regarding complex pelvic masses in pregnancy, MRI becomes the gold standard—but gadolinium is generally contraindicated. This technical deep-dive reviews how non-contrast T1/T2 fat-sat sequences can differentiate between decidualized endometriomas, cystic-degenerating fibroids, and malignancies. We analyze the specific MRI findings in this case that guided the surgical team despite the lack of contrast enhancement.

blogs.title: Partial Myomectomy During Pregnancy: Why Leaving Masses Behind Can Save Lives
blogs.description: The instinct to remove all pathology surgically can be dangerous during pregnancy. This post explores the strategic decision to perform a targeted resection of a pedunculated, torsed upper mass while leaving a fixed pelvic mass *in situ*. We examine the obstetric risks associated with extensive uterine manipulation during gestation versus waiting for postpartum involution when myoma size naturally decreases by nearly half.

blogs.title: From Laparotomy to C-Section: Planning Delivery Routes When Pelvic Anatomy is Distorted by Fibroids
blogs.description: How do you plan for delivery when a pelvic mass acts as a mechanical obstruction? This blog post discusses the long-term planning required after a mid-pregnancy myomectomy. It covers criteria for choosing between vaginal delivery and Cesarean section based on mass location (e.g., posterior wall vs. lower segment), scar integrity from prior surgery, and fetal head engagement risks, advocating for planned C-sections when pelvic outlet obstruction is anticipated.
